Note. All figures are subject to revision. All results
measure percentage change for period, year-on-year, except
where listed as being in crowns. All percentage changes, and
total amount listed in real, inflation adjusted terms.
The CSU changed the methodology for calculating the
inflation adjusted real amount in billions of crowns at the
beginning of the year. All figures use 1994 as a base.
The CSU has not released the real percentage changes for
1995 re-calculated using the new methodology. Nominal 1995
figures using the new methodology -- 1989 was the previous base
REVISED 1995 CZECH GDP Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 1995
Note. Above inflation adjusted figures use new methodology
with 1994 prices as the base. Deflator used for 1995 real GDP
results was 10.1 percent, compared with 7.9 percent for the
first quarter and 9.1 percent for the second quarter 1996.
Czech 1995 GDP, using the old methodolgy grew 4.8 percent,
with growth of 3.9 percent in the first quarter, 4.0 percent in
the second quarter. The CSU did not release a figure under the
old methodology for the third quarter of 1996.

Note. January basket component changes in brackets. All
changes are rises except where stated. Prices have risen 24.1
percent from the average level for 1994 while the sliding
average in February using a 1993 base was 8.6 percent. Basket
of goods and services is unchanged from 1995.
The CSU said in a statement that seasonal influences
accounted for 0.039 percent of the month-on-month figure,
putting seasonally-adjusted growth at 0.377 percent. It added
that core inflaiton was 0.333 percent for the month and that
the influence of price deregulation was 0.044 percent.

CZECH M2 MONEY NOV 1996 OCT 1996 NOV 1995 pct
1996 figures subject to revision. Czech M2 measures currency,
demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign
currency deposits. The bottom figures exlude the effect of SPT
Telecom's $1.32 billion equity expansion in the summer of 1995
which was put on deposit at the Czech National Bank (CNB). The
CNB statement said that total crown and foreign currency
credits obtained by bank clients grew by 10.5 percent,
year-on-year, following 10.7 percent year-on-year growth in
October. It added that total crown and foreign currency
deposits at banks, including funds from SPT Telecom, grew by
growth in October. The statement said the average interest rate
on new crown credits drawn at banks in November was 13.86
percent, some eight basis points higher than October.
